words.gloss: by proclaiming omniscience and association with deities

hindi: विजिगीषु, शत्रु के ग्राम को पाने की इच्छा वाला, सर्वज्ञता और देवताओं के साथ सम्बन्ध की घोषणा से अपने पक्ष को हर्षित करे और शत्रु के पक्ष को उद्विग्न करे।
english: The conqueror, desiring to obtain an enemy's village, should elate his own party by proclaiming [his] omniscience and [his] association with deities, and should alarm the enemy's party.
notes: para = 'other/enemy's' (rendered 'enemy's' as the context is hostile). grāma rendered literally as 'village'; it may mean a settlement or territory generally. The compound sarvajña-daivata-saṃyoga-khyāpana is read as two proclamations (of omniscience; of association with deities), as units 2 and 3 describe them separately. The e-text writes 'samyoga' with m; split restores ṃ.
lines_deva: विजिगीषुः पर.ग्रामम् अवाप्तु.कामः सर्वज्ञ.दैवत.सम्योग.ख्यापनाभ्यां स्व.पक्षम् उद्धर्षयेत्, पर.पक्षं च-उद्वेजयेत्
lines_iast: vijigīṣuḥ para.grāmam avāptu.kāmaḥ sarvajña.daivata.samyoga.khyāpanābhyāṃ sva.pakṣam uddharṣayet, para.pakṣaṃ ca-udvejayet

words.gloss: by knowledge of secret doings in houses
by knowledge through spies of the removal of thorns
of those who do what the king dislikes
proclamation of the present to be reported
by unseen contact, lore, signals and so on

hindi: सर्वज्ञता की घोषणा तो — घरों की गुप्त घटनाओं के ज्ञान से मुखियों का निर्देश करना; कण्टक-शोधन के गुप्तचरों से प्राप्त जानकारी द्वारा राजा के अप्रिय कार्य करने वालों को प्रकट करना; अदृष्ट सम्पर्क, विद्या, संकेत आदि के द्वारा बताए जाने योग्य उपहार की घोषणा; और विदेश की घटनाओं का ज्ञान उसी दिन मुहर से युक्त घरेलू कबूतर के द्वारा।
english: The proclamation of omniscience, however, [consists in]: through knowledge of the secret doings in houses, the pointing out of the chiefs; through knowledge [obtained] from the spies of the removal of thorns, the exposure of those who do what the king dislikes; the proclamation of the present to be reported, by unseen contact, lore, signals and the like; and knowledge of events abroad on that very day, by a house-pigeon furnished with a seal.
notes: The lone '-' token is punctuation in the e-text. pratyādeśa: literally 'pointing out, declaration' (also 'rejection'); medium confidence; 'mukhyānām' is a genitive ('of the chiefs'), rendered 'to the chiefs'. kaṇṭaka-śodhana: literally 'cleansing/removal of thorns'. vijñāpya-upāyana: obscure; literally 'present (upāyana) to be reported/made known (vijñāpya)'; alternative: 'what is to be reported and the present'. adṛṣṭa-saṃsarga: 'unseen contact'; vidyā: 'lore/knowledge'; sañjñā: 'signal/sign'. mudrā rendered 'seal' here (not 'pass' as in 10.1). The e-text writes 'samyuktena' with m. Reviewer: mukhyānām is read as objective genitive, parallel to rāja-dviṣṭa-kāriṇām. vijñāpya may also be the absolutive 'having informed' (vijñāpya upāyana-khyāpanam = proclaiming the present after informing); pratyādeśa and this compound are uncertain, so confidence is effectively low for these two clauses.
lines_deva: सर्वज्ञ.ख्यापनं तु - गृह.गुह्य.प्रवृत्ति.ज्ञानेन प्रत्यादेशो मुख्यानाम्, कण्टक.शोधन.अपसर्प.अवगमेन प्रकाशनं राज.द्विष्ट.कारिणाम्, विज्ञाप्य.उपायन.ख्यापनम् अदृष्ट.संसर्ग.विद्या.सञ्ज्ञा.आदिभिः, विदेश.प्रवृत्ति.ज्ञानं तद् अहर् एव गृह.कपोतेन मुद्रा.सम्युक्तेन
lines_iast: sarvajña.khyāpanaṃ tu - gṛha.guhya.pravṛtti.jñānena pratyādeśo mukhyānām, kaṇṭaka.śodhana.apasarpa.avagamena prakāśanaṃ rāja.dviṣṭa.kāriṇām, vijñāpya.upāyana.khyāpanam adṛṣṭa.saṃsarga.vidyā.sañjñā.ādibhiḥ, videśa.pravṛtti.jñānaṃ tad ahar eva gṛha.kapotena mudrā.samyuktena

words.gloss: through the mouth of a tunnel
hollows of the images of fire, shrine and deity
in the guise of fire, shrine and deity
in the guise of Nagas and Varuna
sight of a garland of fire
by fats of spotted deer, intestine, crab, crocodile, porpoise, otter

hindi: देवताओं के साथ सम्बन्ध की घोषणा तो — सुरंग के मुख से अग्नि, चैत्य और देवता की प्रतिमाओं के छिद्रों में प्रविष्ट हुए, अग्नि, चैत्य और देवता के वेश वालों द्वारा सम्भाषण और पूजन; अथवा जल से उठे हुए, नाग और वरुण के वेश वालों द्वारा सम्भाषण और पूजन; रात में जल के भीतर समुद्र की बालू का कोश रखकर अग्नि-माला का दर्शन; पत्थर और सींके से थामे हुए बेड़े पर टिके रहना; अथवा जल की मशक या जरायु से सिर ढके हुए, नाक छिपाए हुए, चितकबरे मृग, आँत, केकड़े, मगर, शिंशुमार और ऊदबिलाव की चर्बियों से, अथवा सौ बार पकाए हुए तेल का नाक से प्रयोग।
english: The proclamation of association with deities, however, [consists in]: conversation and worship by [agents] in the guise of fire, shrine and deity who have entered, through the mouth of a tunnel, the hollows of the images of the fire, shrine and deity; or conversation and worship by [agents] risen out of the water in the guise of Nagas and Varuna; at night, having placed a sea-sand receptacle inside the water, the sight of a garland of fire; staying on a raft held by a stone and a sling; or, with the head [covered] by a water-bladder or by afterbirth-membrane and the nose concealed, by the fats of the spotted deer, intestine, crab, crocodile, porpoise and otter, or the application through the nose of oil cooked a hundred times.
notes: Several obscure items rendered literally. suruṅgā = tunnel (glossary). chidrān is masculine acc. pl. in the e-text (chidra is normally neuter); kept. 'agni-caitya-daivata' read as three members (fire, shrine, deity); an alternative is 'the deity of the fire-shrine'. kośa here 'receptacle' (not treasury); samudra-vālukā-kośa is unclear (a container of sea-sand). darśana 'sight' (could be 'appearance/display'). śikya = rope-sling/net; plavaka = raft/float. jarāyu = afterbirth/embryonic membrane (alternative: any membrane/skin). 'śiro ''vagūḍha-nāsaḥ': śiraḥ is kept as a separate word ('the head') and avagūḍha-nāsaḥ as 'nose concealed'; whether the head is the thing covered by the bladder/membrane is not stated. The compound pṛṣata-antra-kulīra-nakra-śiṃśumāra-udra-vasābhiḥ is read as 'fats of' all members; whether antra ('intestine') goes only with pṛṣata, and how the second vā divides 'fats' from 'oil cooked a hundred times', is unclear. nastaḥ = through the nose (adverb); śata-pākya = cooked a hundred times. Animal names kept literal, nothing identified. Continues in units 4 and 5. Reviewer: vasābhiḥ is instrumental, so the fats are 'by/with', not the object; a possible reading is 'oil cooked a hundred times with the fats of ... (applied) through the nose'. The Hindi 'सिर ढके हुए' states the covering that English brackets as [covered]; both are inferred. Confidence stays low.
lines_deva: दैवत.सम्योग.ख्यापनं तु - सुरुङ्गा.मुखेन-अग्नि.चैत्य.दैवत.प्रतिमाच्.छिद्रान् अनुप्रविष्टैर् अग्नि.चैत्य.दैवत.व्यञ्जनैः सम्भाषणं पूजनं च, उदकाद् उत्थितैर् वा नाग.वरुण.व्यञ्जनैः सम्भाषणं पूजनं च, रात्राव् अन्तर्.उदके समुद्र.वालुका.कोशं प्रणिधाय-अग्नि.माला.दर्शनम्, शिला.शिक्य.अवगृहीते प्लवके स्थानम्, उदक.बस्तिना जरायुणा वा शिरो ऽवगूढ.नासः पृषत.अन्त्र.कुलीर.नक्र.शिंशुमार.उद्रवसाभिर् वा शत.पाक्यं तैलं नस्तः प्रयोगः
lines_iast: daivata.samyoga.khyāpanaṃ tu - suruṅgā.mukhena-agni.caitya.daivata.pratimāc.chidrān anupraviṣṭair agni.caitya.daivata.vyañjanaiḥ sambhāṣaṇaṃ pūjanaṃ ca, udakād utthitair vā nāga.varuṇa.vyañjanaiḥ sambhāṣaṇaṃ pūjanaṃ ca, rātrāv antar.udake samudra.vālukā.kośaṃ praṇidhāya-agni.mālā.darśanam, śilā.śikya.avagṛhīte plavake sthānam, udaka.bastinā jarāyuṇā vā śiro 'vagūḍha.nāsaḥ pṛṣata.antra.kulīra.nakra.śiṃśumāra.udravasābhir vā śata.pākyaṃ tailaṃ nastaḥ prayogaḥ

hindi: उससे रात्रि-गण विचरण करता है।
english: By that, the night-troop moves about.
notes: Continues unit 3. rātri-gaṇa literally 'night-troop/company'; its exact sense is unclear. 'tena' could also be read 'by that [means]'.
lines_deva: तेन रात्रि.गणश् चरति
lines_iast: tena rātri.gaṇaś carati

hindi: इस प्रकार जल-विचरण।
english: Thus [are] the water-goings.
notes: Closes the list of units 3-4; iti is rendered 'thus' (not a quoted view). caraṇa literally 'going, moving about'; udaka-caraṇa = movements in the water.
lines_deva: इत्य् उदक.चरणानि
lines_iast: ity udaka.caraṇāni

words.gloss: making of speeches of Varuna and the Naga maidens

hindi: उनके द्वारा वरुण और नाग-कन्याओं के वाक्यों की क्रिया और सम्भाषण; क्रोध के अवसरों पर मुख से अग्नि और धुएँ का निकलना।
english: By them, the making of speeches of Varuna and the Naga maidens, and conversation; on occasions of anger, the emission of fire and smoke from the mouth.
notes: 'taiḥ' = those who go about in the water (units 3-5). vākya-kriyā literally 'doing of speech'. varuṇa-nāga-kanyā read as 'Varuna and the Naga maidens'; alternative 'the Naga maidens of Varuna'. sthāna literally 'place'; rendered 'occasions'.
lines_deva: तैर् वरुण.नाग.कन्या.वाक्य.क्रिया सम्भाषणं च, कोप.स्थानेषु मुखाद् अग्नि.धूम.उत्सर्गः
lines_iast: tair varuṇa.nāga.kanyā.vākya.kriyā sambhāṣaṇaṃ ca, kopa.sthāneṣu mukhād agni.dhūma.utsargaḥ

words.gloss: fortune-teller, omen-reader, astrologer, Purana-reciter, observer, secret agents

hindi: अपने देश में ज्योतिषी, नैमित्तिक, मौहूर्तिक, पौराणिक, ईक्षणिक, गूढ़ पुरुष, सहायता करने वाले और उसे देखने वाले, उसकी वह बात प्रकट करें।
english: In his own country, fortune-tellers, omen-readers, astrologers, Purana-reciters, observers, secret agents, those who render assistance, and those who have seen that, should make known that [about] him.

text_flags.why: possible: the word is normally īkṣaṇika (from √īkṣ, 'look'), with long ī; the e-text has short i

notes: sva-viṣaye: 'in his own country' (the conqueror's own). 'tad asya' = 'that of his'. kārtāntika = fortune-teller (glossary); naimittika = reader of omens (nimitta); mauhūrtika = astrologer (glossary); paurāṇika = one versed in the old lore (Purana); īkṣaṇika obscure, literally 'one who looks/observes' (alternative: a physiognomist or diviner by observation) – medium/low confidence. gūḍha-puruṣa = secret agent. sācivya-kara: literally 'those who do the work of an assistant/minister'.
lines_deva: तद् अस्य स्व.विषये कार्तान्तिक.नैमित्तिक.मौहूर्तिक.पौराणिक.इक्षणिक.गूढ.पुरुषाः साचिव्य.करास् तद्.दर्शिनश् च प्रकाशयेयुः
lines_iast: tad asya sva.viṣaye kārtāntika.naimittika.mauhūrtika.paurāṇika.ikṣaṇika.gūḍha.puruṣāḥ sācivya.karās tad.darśinaś ca prakāśayeyuḥ

words.gloss: arising of divine treasury and army

hindi: शत्रु के देश में उसके देवता-दर्शन की और दिव्य कोश और दण्ड की उत्पत्ति की बात कहें।
english: In the enemy's country, they should tell of his sight of deities and of the arising of a divine treasury and army.
notes: parasya viṣaye = in the other's (enemy's) country. daṇḍa = army, kośa = treasury (glossary). divya could also qualify only kośa; read with kośa-daṇḍa.
lines_deva: परस्य विषये दैवत.दर्शनं दिव्य.कोश.दण्ड.उत्पत्तिं च-अस्य ब्रूयुः
lines_iast: parasya viṣaye daivata.darśanaṃ divya.kośa.daṇḍa.utpattiṃ ca-asya brūyuḥ

words.gloss: in questions to deities, omens, crows, lore of limbs, dreams, cries of beasts and birds

hindi: देवताओं से प्रश्न, शकुन, कौए, अंग-विद्या, स्वप्न तथा पशु-पक्षियों की बोलियों में उसकी विजय बताएँ, और शत्रु का विपरीत बताएँ।
english: In questions to deities, omens, crows, the lore of limbs, dreams, and the cries of beasts and birds, they should tell of his victory, [they should tell] the reverse of the enemy's.
notes: The long compound is split into members as listed; the grouping is uncertain (e.g. vāyasa-aṅga-vidyā could be one item 'crow- and limb-lore'; vyāhāra may belong only to mṛga-pakṣi). daivata-praśna: 'questions to/about deities' (consulting deities). nimitta = omens. The predicate of the last phrase is understood from the preceding clause ('[they should tell] the reverse of the enemy'); supplied in brackets in English.
lines_deva: दैवत.प्रश्न.निमित्त.वायस.अङ्ग.विद्या.स्वप्न.मृग.पक्षि.व्याहारेषु च-अस्य विजयं ब्रूयुः, विपरीतम् अमित्रस्य
lines_iast: daivata.praśna.nimitta.vāyasa.aṅga.vidyā.svapna.mṛga.pakṣi.vyāhāreṣu ca-asya vijayaṃ brūyuḥ, viparītam amitrasya

hindi: और शत्रु के नक्षत्र में दुन्दुभि के साथ उल्का दिखाएँ।
english: And they should show a meteor accompanied by a drum in the enemy's nakṣatra (lunar mansion).
notes: sa-dundubhi: 'accompanied by a drum' (perhaps a drum-like sound); the i-stem bahuvrīhi agrees with the feminine ulkā. nakṣatre could also be 'under the star/asterism' of the enemy; literal 'in the nakṣatra'. ca joins sadundubhim and ulkām as one phrase. Reviewer: ca here connects this sentence with the preceding one ('and ... a meteor'); sadundubhim qualifies ulkām.
lines_deva: सदुन्दुभिम् उल्कां च परस्य नक्षत्रे दर्शयेयुः
lines_iast: sadundubhim ulkāṃ ca parasya nakṣatre darśayeyuḥ

words.gram: m. nom. pl., pres. part. upa-√diś

words.gloss: bestowal of strength on own party

hindi: दूत के वेश वाले गुप्तचर, शत्रु के मुख्यों को मित्र के रूप में बताते हुए, स्वामी के सत्कार को, अपने पक्ष को बल देने को और शत्रु के पक्ष के प्रतिघात को कहें।
english: Agents in the guise of envoys, pointing out the enemy's chiefs as allies, should tell of the king's honouring [of them], the bestowal of strength on his own party and the repulse of the enemy's party.
notes: svāmi = king (glossary); svāmi-satkāra could be 'honour from the king' (the conqueror) or 'honour of the king'; rendered 'the king's honouring'. upadiś: 'point out, designate'. bala = strength (could be 'troops'). pratighāta = repulse/warding off (alternative: destruction). The vyañjana agents are secret agents (glossary: X-vyañjana).
lines_deva: परस्य मुख्यान् मित्रत्वेन-उपदिशन्तो दूत.व्यञ्जनाः स्वामि.सत्कारं ब्रूयुः, स्व.पक्ष.बल.आधानं पर.पक्ष.प्रतिघातं च
lines_iast: parasya mukhyān mitratvena-upadiśanto dūta.vyañjanāḥ svāmi.satkāraṃ brūyuḥ, sva.pakṣa.bala.ādhānaṃ para.pakṣa.pratighātaṃ ca

words.gram: n. acc. sg., tulya + samāhāra-dvandva yoga-kṣema

hindi: अमात्यों और शस्त्रजीवियों के समान योग और क्षेम को कहें।
english: They should relate the equal acquisition and security of the ministers and of the men of arms.
notes: yoga-kṣema follows the glossary (6.2: acquisition and security); it may also mean 'welfare, livelihood'. āyudhīya = one who lives by weapons (soldier); rendered 'men of arms'. Whose yoga-kṣema (the conqueror's grant to the enemy's ministers and soldiers, or among them) is not stated; the genitives are rendered literally.
lines_deva: तुल्य.योग.क्षेमम् अमात्यानाम् आयुधीयानां च कथयेयुः
lines_iast: tulya.yoga.kṣemam amātyānām āyudhīyānāṃ ca kathayeyuḥ

hindi: उनके प्रति व्यसन और अभ्युदय में ध्यान तथा सन्तान का सम्मान प्रयोग में लाए।
english: Towards them, he should apply attention to [their] calamity and prosperity and the honouring of [their] children.
notes: teṣu = the ministers and men of arms of unit 12. vyasana = calamity (glossary). avekṣaṇa = looking after, regard. 'their' is supplied in brackets.
lines_deva: तेषु व्यसन.अभ्युदय.अवेक्षणम् अपत्य.पूजनं च प्रयुञ्जीत
lines_iast: teṣu vyasana.abhyudaya.avekṣaṇam apatya.pūjanaṃ ca prayuñjīta

hindi: उससे शत्रु के पक्ष को उभारे, जैसा पहले कहा गया है।
english: By that, he should rouse the enemy's party, as said before.
notes: utsāhayet literally 'make eager/rouse'; here 'incite'. tena may mean 'by that means' (the foregoing measures).
lines_deva: तेन पर.पक्षम् उत्साहयेद् यथा.उक्तं पुरस्तात्
lines_iast: tena para.pakṣam utsāhayed yathā.uktaṃ purastāt

hindi: और हम और भी कहेंगे।
english: And we shall say more.
notes: bhūyas = further/again.
lines_deva: भूयश् च वक्ष्यामः
lines_iast: bhūyaś ca vakṣyāmaḥ

words.gloss: by striking with club and branch
by a cloud born of deceit
by the ornament of the unfortunate

hindi: साधारण गधे से कुशलों को, लाठी और शाखा के प्रहार से दण्ड-चारियों को, और कुल के मेढ़े से उद्विग्नों को, अशनि की वर्षा से अपमानितों को, विदुल, अवकेशी, कौए के पिण्ड और छल से उत्पन्न मेघ से, इस प्रकार निराश हुओं को, अभागे के आभूषण और द्वेषी से, इस प्रकार सम्मान के फल वालों को, बाघ की खाल और मृत्यु-जाल से रखे हुओं को, पीलु के खाने, करक-योष्ट्रा और गधी के दूध के मथने से, इस प्रकार सदा उपकार करने वालों को, इस प्रकार।
english: The skilled, by a common ass; the staff-goers, by striking with club and branch; and the agitated, by a family ram; the dishonoured, by a rain of thunderbolts; those whose hopes are shattered, by vidula, avakeśin, a crow's ball and a cloud born of deceit, thus; those whose fruit is honour, by an ornament of the unfortunate and by a hostile one, thus; the placed, by a tiger-skin and a death-trap; the always helpful, by the eating of pīlu, by karaka-yoṣṭrā and by the churning of she-ass's milk, thus; thus.

text_flags.why: possible: yoṣṭrā is not a known word; yoktra ('rope, thong') is the usual form; the printed form is kept in the split

notes: Very obscure passage; the text has no governing verb, and each phrase pairs a class of persons (accusative) with a means (instrumental). It is rendered literally and word by word; the relation between the classes and the means is not clear, and iti marks the end of each group of means (and, at the very end, of the whole list) – rendered 'thus', not as a quoted view. sādhāraṇa = common/shared/ordinary; daṇḍa-cārin = literally 'going with a staff' (alternative: 'moving with the army/punishment'); kula-eḍaka = ram of the family (alternative: 'a ram/sheep of good family'); vidula, avakeśin, pīlu and karaka names kept (vidula perhaps a cane; avakeśin unclear; pīlu may be a tree/fruit; karaka perhaps a water-pot or hail); vāyasa-piṇḍa = 'crow's ball/lump'; kaitava-ja-megha = 'cloud born of deceit/trickery' (kaitava may also name a plant); durbhaga = unfortunate/unlucky; dveṣin = hating/hostile; pūjā-phala = having honour as fruit; upahita = placed/provided (alternative: entrapped, deceived); kūṭa = trap (also deceit, peak); vikhādana = eating up/devouring; yoṣṭrā see text_flags. dhruva-upakārin = constantly benefiting. Possibly these are devices by which the classes of persons are told apart or approached; the draft does not claim this. Reviewer: in the Sanskrit each iti follows a list of means and precedes the next class (vihata-āśān, pūjā-phalān) or closes the list (final iti); the English moves the class first. 'thus' is the bare literal sense and its function is unknown. upahita, durbhaga-alaṅkāra and dveṣin (adjective of alaṅkāreṇa or a separate 'hostile one') have unresolved readings.
lines_deva: साधारण.गर्दभेन दक्षान्, लकुट.शाखा.हननाभ्यां दण्ड.चारिणः, कुल.एडकेन च-उद्विग्नान्, अशनि.वर्षेण विमानितान्, विदुलेन-अवकेशिना वायस.पिण्डेन कैतवज.मेघेन-इति विहत.आशान् दुर्भग.अलङ्कारेण द्वेषिणा-इति पूजा.फलान्, व्याघ्र.चर्मणा मृत्यु.कूटेन च-उपहितान्, पीलु.विखादनेन करक.योष्ट्रया गर्दभी.क्षीरा.अभिमन्थनेन-इति ध्रुव.उपकारिण इति
lines_iast: sādhāraṇa.gardabhena dakṣān, lakuṭa.śākhā.hananābhyāṃ daṇḍa.cāriṇaḥ, kula.eḍakena ca-udvignān, aśani.varṣeṇa vimānitān, vidulena-avakeśinā vāyasa.piṇḍena kaitavaja.meghena-iti vihata.āśān durbhaga.alaṅkāreṇa dveṣiṇā-iti pūjā.phalān, vyāghra.carmaṇā mṛtyu.kūṭena ca-upahitān, pīlu.vikhādanena karaka.yoṣṭrayā gardabhī.kṣīrā.abhimanthanena-iti dhruva.upakāriṇa iti

hindi: स्वीकार कर चुके लोगों को धन और मान से युक्त करे।
english: He should provide those who have accepted with wealth and honour.
notes: pratipanna: 'agreed, accepted, come over' (alternative: 'obtained'). yojayet literally 'should join/endow'.
lines_deva: प्रतिपन्नान् अर्थ.मानाभ्यां योजयेत्
lines_iast: pratipannān artha.mānābhyāṃ yojayet

words.gloss: in gaps of goods and food
with gifts of goods and food

hindi: और द्रव्य तथा भोजन की कमियों में इन पर द्रव्य और भोजन के दान से अनुग्रह करे।
english: And in the gaps of goods and food, he should favour them with gifts of goods and food.
notes: chidra literally 'gap, hole, weak point'; rendered 'gaps' (probably times of shortage). The c in bhaktac.chidreṣu is the euphonic doubling before ch. enān = those of unit 17.
lines_deva: द्रव्य.भक्तच्.छिद्रेषु च-एनान् द्रव्य.भक्त.दानैर् अनुगृह्णीयात्
lines_iast: dravya.bhaktac.chidreṣu ca-enān dravya.bhakta.dānair anugṛhṇīyāt

words.gram: m. gen. pl., pres. part. neg.

hindi: जो स्वीकार नहीं करते उन्हें स्त्रियों और कुमारों के आभूषण ले आएँ।
english: To those who do not accept, they should bring ornaments of women and boys.
notes: The genitive apratigṛhṇatām is rendered 'to' (dative sense); abhi-√hṛ literally 'bring to'; 'abhi-√hṛ' may also mean 'present, offer'. What is not accepted is not stated (presumably the gifts of unit 18). kumāra = boy/youth (also prince).
lines_deva: अप्रतिगृह्णतां स्त्री.कुमार.अलङ्कारान् अभिहरेयुः
lines_iast: apratigṛhṇatāṃ strī.kumāra.alaṅkārān abhihareyuḥ

words.gloss: in the harms of famine, thieves and forest tribes

words.gram: m. nom. pl., pres. part. caus. ud-√sah

hindi: दुर्भिक्ष, चोरों और वन-जातियों के उपघातों में नगरवासियों और जनपदवासियों को उभारते हुए गुप्तचर कहें — "हम राजा से अनुग्रह माँगते हैं; अनुग्रह के बिना हम अन्यत्र जाते हैं।"
english: In the harms of famine, thieves and forest tribes, the secret agents, rousing the townsmen and country people, should say: "We ask the king for favour; without favour, we go elsewhere."
notes: Closing iti closes the quotation and is not translated separately (glossary). utsāhayantaḥ literally 'making eager/rousing'. yāc takes two accusatives (rājānam, anugraham). paratra can also mean 'in the next world'; 'elsewhere' fits here. upaghāta = harm/injury. Glossary: sattrin = secret agent; paura = townsmen; jānapada = country people; aṭavī = forest tribes.
lines_deva: दुर्भिक्ष.स्तेन.अटव्य्.उपघातेषु च पौर.जानपदान् उत्साहयन्तः सत्त्रिणो ब्रूयुः "राजानम् अनुग्रहं याचामहे- निरनुग्रहाः परत्र गच्छामः" इति
lines_iast: durbhikṣa.stena.aṭavy.upaghāteṣu ca paura.jānapadān utsāhayantaḥ sattriṇo brūyuḥ "rājānam anugrahaṃ yācāmahe- niranugrahāḥ paratra gacchāmaḥ" iti

hindi: "वैसा ही" — यह स्वीकार कर चुकने पर, द्रव्य और धान्य, अपरिग्रहों से; "सहायता करनी चाहिए" — उपजाप से यह महान् उत्पन्न हुआ।
english: When they have agreed, [saying] "So be it": goods and grains, by non-acceptances; "assistance is to be rendered" – this great [result] has arisen from secret instigation.
notes: Line a has no finite verb; the syntax is uncertain and the reading is low confidence. aparigraha = non-acceptance/non-possession (alternatives: 'without taking', or a split dhānya-anya-parigrahaiḥ 'grains, other possessions' is not supported by the printed text). dravya-dhānyāni is nominative/accusative plural, left without a governing word. sācivya = assistance (alternative: ministership). bhūta mahat: 'a great [thing/result] arisen'; the substantive is not stated. upajāpa = secret instigation (glossary). Metre: anuṣṭubh-like verse of two lines.
lines_deva: तथा-इति प्रतिपन्नेषु द्रव्य.धान्यान्य् अपरिग्रहैः
साचिव्यं कार्यम् इत्य् एतद् उपजापाद् भूतं महत्
lines_iast: tathā-iti pratipanneṣu dravya.dhānyāny aparigrahaiḥ
sācivyaṃ kāryam ity etad upajāpād bhūtaṃ mahat
